subproblem.title: An extension to ℝ^P with support in a compact K ⊂ U has no more mass or boundary mass than its restriction to U
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and K ⊆ U compact. Let X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) and Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (m + 1)) be currents such that (a) Y restricts to X, i.e. Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X: Y(ιη) = X(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U), where ι = testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) regards a test form in U (TestFormOn U (m + 1): a smooth form on ℝ^P with compact support contained in U) as a test form on ℝ^P without changing it; and (b) spt Y ⊆ K, where spt is the support of Simon 6.2.11 (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then M(Y) ≤ M(X) and M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X). Here ∂ is GeometricCurrentOn.boundary (∂Z(ω) = Z(dω)); M(Y) = Y.mass = Y.massOn ℝ^P and M(X) = X.mass = X.massOn U, where Z.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(Z(ω)) over test forms ω in the domain of Z with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x (Simon 6.2.4–6.2.5).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X → Y.support ⊆ K → Y.mass ≤ X.mass ∧ Y.boundary.mass ≤ X.boundary.mass
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7–8 of the parent proof, by the cutoff argument of step 8. This is also the argument of the grandparent proof's step 3(c), Simon Ch. 6 proof of Theorem 7.2: X̂(ω) = X(ζω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U; [0, 1]) equal to 1 near K, and masses do not increase. The parent reuses dtc_extend_by_zero, which yields Y with its restriction to U, the bound spt Y ⊆ K and IsIntegerMultiplicity Y, but no explicit representation of Y by (M ∩ K, θ, ξ). That forces two adaptations here:
(1) Step 8 reads the locality "Y(ω) = Y(ω') when ω = ω' near K" off the integral formula of step 4. Here it comes from the sibling vanish_off_support, Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Z = ∅, applied to Y with spt Y ⊆ K.
(2) The parent text gets the mass bound of step 7 from (ME) and a representation of Y. Here it is proved by the same cutoff argument in degree m + 1.
Notation. ι_d := testFormOnInclusion (subset_univ U) d : 𝒟^d(U) → 𝒟^d(ℝ^P); it does not change the underlying form. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}, summed over strictly increasing I : Fin d → Fin P, with e_I = (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(d−1)}) from the standard basis. A test form ω on G is admissible for M_W when tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; M_W(Z) = Z.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(Z(ω)) over admissible ω. Currents are linear on test forms. The hypothesis Y.restrictDomain (subset_univ U) = X means Y(ι_{m+1}η) = X(η) for every η ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply).
1. (Cutoff.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ > 0 with K_δ := cthickening δ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K_δ is closed (isClosed_cthickening) and compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper). Also K ⊆ thickening δ K ⊆ interior K_δ (self_subset_thickening, thickening_subset_interior_cthickening), and K is closed. Apply the smooth Urysohn lemma exists_contMDiffMap_one_nhds_of_subset_interior (model 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), smoothness ⊤ : ℕ∞, s := K, t := K_δ), then contMDiff_iff_contDiff. This gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 everywhere, ζ(x) = 0 for x ∉ K_δ, and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K. By mem_nhdsSet_iff_exists there is an open O ⊇ K with ζ = 1 on O. Since {ζ ≠ 0} ⊆ K_δ and K_δ is closed, tsupport ζ ⊆ K_δ (closure_minimal). So ζ has compact support (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset) and tsupport ζ ⊆ U.
2. (Cut-off test forms.) Let d ∈ ℕ, ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), and let ζω be the form x ↦ ζ(x)ω(x).
 (a) ζω is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul), and tsupport(ζω) ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ K_δ ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left). So ζω has compact support and is a test form in U: ζω ∈ 𝒟^d(U).
 (b) For c ∈ ℝ and a d-covector α, (cα)(e_I) = c·α(e_I). So Σ_I (cα)(e_I)² = c²·Σ_I α(e_I)², and |cα| = √(c²S) = |c|·√S = |c|·|α| (Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs). Hence |(ζω)(x)| = ζ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| for every x, as 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1. If |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, then ζω is admissible for M_U: tsupport(ζω) ⊆ U by (a), and |(ζω)(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
 (c) The test form ω − ι_d(ζω) ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) has underlying form x ↦ ω(x) − ζ(x)ω(x). It vanishes on O, where ζ = 1. So its support lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ O, and tsupport(ω − ι_d(ζω)) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ O (closure_minimal). Since spt Y ⊆ K ⊆ O, tsupport(ω − ι_d(ζω)) ∩ spt Y = ∅.
3. (Mass, M(Y) ≤ M(X).) M(Y) = Y.mass = Y.massOn ℝ^P. It is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(Y(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x; the condition tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P is automatic. Fix such an ω and put η := ζω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (step 2(a)). By step 2(c) and vanish_off_support applied to Y, Y(ω − ι_{m+1}η) = 0. By linearity Y(ω) = Y(ι_{m+1}η) = X(η), the last equality by the restriction hypothesis. η is admissible for M_U(X) by step 2(b). Hence ENNReal.ofReal(Y(ω)) = ENNReal.ofReal(X(η)) ≤ X.massOn U = X.mass (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Taking the supremum over ω (sSup_le) gives M(Y) ≤ M(X).
4. (Boundary mass, M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X).) M(∂Y) = Y.boundary.massOn ℝ^P. It is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(∂Y(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Fix such an ω and put η := ζω ∈ 𝒟^m(U); η is admissible for M_U(∂X) by step 2(b).
 - Let d_G := exteriorDerivativeTestOn G m : 𝒟^m(G) → 𝒟^{m+1}(G). It is a linear map, and the underlying form of d_G φ is dφ.
 - By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply and the restriction hypothesis, ∂Y(ω) = Y(d_{ℝ^P} ω) and ∂X(η) = X(d_U η) = Y(ι_{m+1}(d_U η)).
 - The test forms d_{ℝ^P}(ι_m η) and ι_{m+1}(d_U η) have the same underlying form d(ζω), so they are equal. By linearity of d_{ℝ^P}, d_{ℝ^P} ω − ι_{m+1}(d_U η) = d_{ℝ^P}(ω − ι_m η).
 - Its tsupport lies in tsupport(ω − ι_m η) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ O (SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset and step 2(c)), which is disjoint from spt Y.
 - By vanish_off_support, Y(d_{ℝ^P} ω − ι_{m+1}(d_U η)) = 0. By linearity, ∂Y(ω) = Y(d_{ℝ^P} ω) = Y(ι_{m+1}(d_U η)) = ∂X(η).
 Hence ENNReal.ofReal(∂Y(ω)) = ENNReal.ofReal(∂X(η)) ≤ X.boundary.massOn U = X.boundary.mass (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Taking the supremum over ω gives M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X). ∎
proof_key_steps: Smooth Urysohn: a C^∞ ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] equal to 1 on an open O ⊇ K, with tsupport ζ ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ U compact.
For ω on ℝ^P with |ω| ≤ 1, ζω is an admissible test form in U (|ζω| = ζ|ω| ≤ 1), and ω − ζω is supported in ℝ^P ∖ O, disjoint from spt Y ⊆ K.
vanish_off_support and the restriction give Y(ω) = Y(ζω) = X(ζω) ≤ M(X); the supremum gives M(Y) ≤ M(X).
d is linear and tsupport(dφ) ⊆ tsupport φ, so ∂Y(ω) = Y(d(ζω)) = X(d(ζω)) = ∂X(ζω) ≤ M(∂X); the supremum gives M(∂Y) ≤ M(∂X).

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type match for general currents; no integer-multiplicity or finite-mass hypothesis is missing. The cutoff preserves admissibility using the actual Euclidean coefficient norm. Vanishing off support gives equality of current evaluations, and exterior-derivative linearity and support locality give the boundary equality. Taking suprema proves both bounds. The sole dependency on vanish_off_support is correctly directed, and the bare name is unreserved.
